title: Traction & Railway Energy

canonicalTerminology.definition: Tractive effort is the longitudinal force available at the wheel-rail interface to move a train.

claims.text: Traction performance depends on the interaction between power supply or prime mover, traction equipment, vehicle resistance and wheel-rail adhesion.
claims.applicabilityNote: Level-neutral educational statement; adapt depth without changing the canonical fact.

equations.limitation: Ideal mechanical relationship for teaching; efficiencies and system limits must be treated separately.

visualSpecs.purpose: Show energy conversion from supply or fuel to wheel-rail force.

prohibitedUnsupportedClaims: Do not invent operational acceptance limits, tolerances, settings or manufacturer-specific values.
Do not present educational diagrams or summaries as approved operating or maintenance instructions.
